methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series F → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.3x) to $15.0B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in AI & Software. Range: $3.8B - $312.5B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Applied Intuition, a Series F AI & Software company founded by Qasar Younis and Peter Ludwig, is valued at $15.0B post-money following $600M+ in cumulative fundraising. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies (1 public, 8 private) in the AI & Software sector at Series E and adjacent stages, including Palantir, Crusoe Energy, SandboxAQ, and Ayar Labs.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, which models typical Series F to next-stage step-ups, implies a valuation of $19.5B using a 1.3x multiplier applied to the current $15.0B post-money valuation. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $7.9B, though the peer set exhibits substantial dispersion (range: $3.8B to $312.5B), with the wide band reflecting heterogeneity in growth trajectory and market position among AI software companies.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $6.7B (low) to $22.4B (high), with a median implied value of $13.7B. The current $15.0B valuation sits near the median, slightly above it. Key uncertainties include the outsized influence of Palantir at $312.5B within the peer set and the difficulty of isolating stage-specific comparables given the sparse public market representation of frontier-stage AI software businesses. The analysis supports valuations in the $13.7B to $19.5B range under base-case assumptions.
